reviewLabel: Evidence checked 11 September; source publication and observation dates retained.

plants.name: Ramin
plants.location: Bornean peat-swamp habitat. Marker represents the Sebangau region for orientation; it is not a current occurrence survey.
plants.availability: Current wild abundance and nursery stock are unknown. Restoration research documents planting of this species.
plants.parts: Living seed trees, viable seeds and nursery seedlings are the relevant recovery material. Roots and living stem tissue need field assessment after fire.
plants.recovery: Protect surviving seed trees and restore peat hydrology. Specialist nurseries can raise verified local material for suitable peat-swamp sites.
plants.impact: Regional peat fires justify checking surviving populations. No source reviewed identifies current mortality of this species.
plants.riskBasis: Screening inference: this plant belongs on the peat-restoration watchlist while regional peat fires are reported. Its presence in a burned footprint has not been verified.

plants.name: Balangeran
plants.location: Sebangau restoration landscape. Older restoration records use the synonym Shorea balangeran. Marker is a regional reference.
plants.availability: Documented in BNF community nursery planting in 2020; today's seed and seedling stocks are unverified.
plants.parts: Seeds and nursery seedlings; surviving parent trees retain the next generation's seed source.
plants.recovery: Use identified local nursery stock and suitable wetland microsites. Protect planting areas from repeat fire and monitor establishment.
plants.impact: Regional peat fires justify checking surviving populations. No source reviewed identifies current mortality of this species.
plants.riskBasis: Screening inference: this plant belongs on the peat-restoration watchlist while regional peat fires are reported. Its presence in a burned footprint has not been verified.

plants.name: Jelutung rawa
plants.location: Peat-swamp restoration watchlist. Marker represents the Kapuas region; local presence must be verified before site-level decisions.
plants.availability: Published propagation and peatland planting studies exist. No current Kalimantan supplier inventory has been confirmed.
plants.parts: Seeds and seedlings are potential restoration material. The species also produces latex; latex cannot regenerate a tree.
plants.recovery: Raise local seedlings and select peatland habitat suited to the species. Protect young plants and monitor survival; research in Jambi is evidence of a method, not proof of Kalimantan stock.
plants.impact: Regional peat fires justify checking surviving populations. No source reviewed identifies current mortality of this species.
plants.riskBasis: Screening inference: this plant belongs on the peat-restoration watchlist while regional peat fires are reported. Its presence in a burned footprint has not been verified.

plants.name: Gerunggang
plants.location: Sebangau regional restoration reference. BNF's 2020 account documents this taxon among locally grown planting species.
plants.availability: Historical community nursery record; available quantities and survival after current fires are unknown.
plants.parts: Locally sourced seeds and nursery plants. Living stems and roots require inspection before any claim of regeneration.
plants.recovery: Include appropriate local material in a diverse restoration mix. Nursery precedent supports feasibility, but site conditions determine outcomes.
plants.impact: Regional peat fires justify checking surviving populations. No source reviewed identifies current mortality of this species.
plants.riskBasis: Screening inference: this plant belongs on the peat-restoration watchlist while regional peat fires are reported. Its presence in a burned footprint has not been verified.

plants.name: Ulin · Bornean ironwood
plants.location: Lowland Bornean forest watchlist. East Kalimantan anchor is approximate; Kew confirms Borneo within the native range.
plants.availability: Current local population, seed collection and nursery availability are unverified.
plants.parts: Viable seeds, seedlings and surviving parent trees. Durable dead timber does not imply that a fire-damaged tree is alive.
plants.recovery: Prioritize surviving adults and habitat protection. Seedling research finds slow growth, so recovery requires long-term monitoring rather than a 15-day planting outcome.
plants.impact: No current fire report reviewed establishes damage to this species or its cultivated stock.
plants.riskBasis: Current regional fire reporting has not been matched to a verified population of this species. A fire-risk category cannot be assigned to these plants yet.

plants.name: Kasturi · Kalimantan mango
plants.statusLabel: Extinct in the wild · historical status
plants.location: South Kalimantan cultivation context. Marker represents the Banjar / Banjarbaru region, not an identified tree or nursery.
plants.availability: Persists in cultivation according to conservation literature. Today's local stock and fire impacts are unverified.
plants.parts: Living cultivated trees, seeds and nursery plants. Identity and genetic diversity should be checked before propagation or reintroduction.
plants.recovery: Safeguard cultivated material and work with botanical specialists on propagation. Reintroduction needs suitable protected habitat; the EW listing is not evidence of extinction caused by the current fires.
plants.impact: No current fire report reviewed establishes damage to this species or its cultivated stock.
plants.riskBasis: Current regional fire reporting has not been matched to a verified population of this species. A fire-risk category cannot be assigned to these plants yet.

reports.summary: Review of sources available on 9 September: the Forestry Ministry reports declining hotspots in several priority provinces using 8 September observations. Earlier field reports describe a contained sedge fire at Sebangau’s northern boundary and approximately 49.5 hectares affected in Mawas. These are habitat-level signals, not proof of death in any named plant population.
reports.mortality: No new species-level plant deaths, extirpations or extinctions verified in the reviewed sources.
reports.availability: Historical nursery leads remain useful, but today’s seed, seedling and surviving-tree quantities are unknown.
reports.coverage: All five Kalimantan provinces are shown. North Kalimantan has an explicit evidence gap. Map markers are approximate orientation anchors, not verified tree occurrences or burned-area boundaries.

reports.summary: New reports document rotating air operations in East Kalimantan and a cumulative fire record for Penajam Paser Utara through 8 September. These strengthen regional habitat concern without proving overlap with named plant populations.
reports.mortality: No species-level plant deaths, extirpations or new extinctions verified in the sources reviewed today.
reports.availability: Current seed, seedling and surviving-tree quantities remain unverified; historical nursery leads are not live stock listings.
reports.coverage: Five provinces remain visible. North Kalimantan has an evidence gap. Map points are approximate regional references, not individual plants or current fire perimeters.

reports.summary: South Kalimantan now has a newly published cumulative provincial fire assessment through 10 September. Regional habitat concern continues; no new named-plant damage was verified.
reports.mortality: Named plant mortality, local extirpation and new extinction remain unverified.
reports.availability: No live nursery stock or surviving-tree inventory was verified today.
reports.coverage: Approximate regional map references remain unchanged. Province-level fire totals cannot establish overlap with individual plant populations. North Kalimantan remains an evidence gap in this dataset.

monitoring.label: Daily evidence checks scheduled through 23 September

news.title: South Kalimantan cumulative fire footprint reported
news.summary: ANTARA reports BPBD totals of 20,206.06 hectares affected and 2,963 incidents from 1 January through 10 September. This provincial cumulative figure does not establish mortality of kasturi or other named plants.

news.title: Air operations rotate across fire areas
news.summary: ANTARA reports water-bombing operations in Kutai Kartanegara on 9 September after Samarinda on 8 September. Regional response activity does not establish losses of ulin or any other named plant.

news.title: Penajam Paser Utara: cumulative fire impacts
news.summary: BPBD figures reported by ANTARA record 113 incidents and 199.79 hectares affected from January through 8 September. This cumulative district total is not a daily burned-area estimate or a plant mortality count.

news.title: Hotspots declined; suppression continues
news.summary: The Forestry Ministry reports falling high-confidence hotspots in four priority provinces using 8 September observations. West Kalimantan declined from 31 to 12. These are satellite indicators, not counts of burned plants.

news.title: Fire reached Sebangau’s northern boundary
news.summary: BNF reports a fire contained in sedge vegetation, with no primary forest affected in that incident. This does not establish park-wide safety or identify losses of particular trees.

news.title: Mawas conservation area affected
news.summary: BOSF reports approximately 49.5 hectares affected by fire in Mawas. The report describes vegetation and habitat impacts without identifying plant species mortality.

news.title: Peat-fire response in Banjarbaru
news.summary: ANTARA reports efforts to cool and suppress underground peat fires near Pengayuan. The report does not establish damage to cultivated kasturi or other named plants.

regions.name: West Kalimantan
regions.detail: Latest ministry report shows fewer hotspots. Species-level plant records are still needed.

regions.name: Central Kalimantan
regions.detail: Dated field reports document fire at Sebangau’s boundary and in Mawas. Named plant losses remain unverified.

regions.name: South Kalimantan
regions.detail: BPBD reports provincial impacts through 10 September. Damage to kasturi populations has not been established.

regions.name: East Kalimantan
regions.detail: New reporting describes air operations and cumulative impacts in Penajam Paser Utara. Exposure of individual ulin populations remains unverified.

regions.name: North Kalimantan
regions.detail: No current regional source retained in this review. Missing reports do not mean low risk.
